_doc: Explicit named whitelist of PortWalk dispatch discriminators permitted to be COARSE — each carries a reason justifying why it has no semantic projection (it falls to an emit:/pay:/role label no flow rule reads). STATELESS INVARIANT (PortWalkExhaustivenessTests): every discriminator must be EITHER projected (PortWalkProjection) OR named here; a new one that is neither fails loudly. A name here that becomes projected, or that no longer exists, fails until removed. This is a list of NAMES, each justified — not a count and not a moving ratchet. The size is the interaction layer's known-blind-spot metric (see docs/scratch/alignment-session/03-portwalk-exhaustiveness-findings.md).

effectType.attach: INVESTIGATED 2026-07-18 (Currency A pass, port-label-census topProjectionGaps, cardCount 589 / comboPopularityMass 567091). UNLIKE emit:preventable/emit:keywordability, AttachEffect (CR 701.3, 'attach [this permanent] to target [filter]') is NOT a grab-bag — it is a single, well-typed EffectType with a real Target ObjectReference (Equip's keyword expansion in EquipKeyword.cs always emits AttachEffect{Target: creature/planeswalker filter, Controller}, and the explicit-text shapes (AttachTriggeredRule, ReconfigureKeyword, AuraLosesGainsEnchantReturnAndAttachRule) carry the same structured Target). The blocker is NOT coherence — it is that NO consume Role anywhere in PortGraphEngine.FlowFeasible's (ResourceKind(emit), Role(consume)) grammar reads an 'attach' resource, and building one requires a trigger event ('becomes attached to a permanent', CR 701.3d/603.2) that doesn't exist even as an AST enum member (TriggerCondition.cs has BecomesUnattached — itself already coarse-whitelisted and unconsumed — but no BecomesAttached at all), so real cards that say it verbatim (Psychic Paper: 'As this Equipment becomes attached to a creature, choose...'; Assimilation Aegis: 'Whenever this Equipment becomes attached to a creature...') can't even be discriminated today. Sampled every corpus combo shape carrying this label (Thornbite Staff, Nim Deathmantle, Breath of Fury / SacrificeAttachThenUntapAllAndAdditionalCombatRule, Ronin Warclub/Ancestral Katana/Sword of the Meek/Dredging Claw/Stormrider Rig's re-equip-on-ETB family): in every case the attach is bookkeeping ALONGSIDE the actual loop driver (a granted tap ability + death-untap, a graveyard reanimation already projecting the real emit:returntobattlefield, or emit:additionalcombat) — none of them need attach itself to be a flow edge; the loop already closes through an existing arm. Arming attach with a faithful Target-filter Subject today would therefore produce a well-typed but ORPHAN emit no FlowFeasible clause reads — zero new edges, defeating Currency A's purpose ('one arm lights up every card') — because attaching is a STATE/positional predicate (CR 701.3), not a flow resource (mana/life/token/damage/counters) in ADR-0002's grammar, and inventing a Role for it is an engine-taxonomy decision, not a Currency-A arm. Per adding-a-flow-arm.md anti-patterns + INTERACTION.md's parse-inside-engine-bridge stop condition: scoped down, did not force an arm; consciously left coarse. Re-pick either as a dedicated Parse-track slice adding a BecomesAttached TriggerEvent (unlocks Psychic Paper/Assimilation Aegis as single-card witnesses first, no combo needed) followed by a proper engine-taxonomy decision on what Role it feeds, or leave dormant — do not smuggle a state-predicate through the resource-flow grammar.

effectType.keywordAbility: INVESTIGATED 2026-07-18 (Currency A pass, port-label-census topProjectionGaps, 2nd-highest comboPopularityMass after emit:unparsed): KeywordAbilityEffect is the SHARED terminal node for every parameterless CR 702 keyword MAST leaves undecomposed — 178 Keywords/Definitions/*.cs files exist, 95 of which are Definition=>null / "combinator-only" (their own doc comments say e.g. "MAST records the keyword's presence; the exile-and-cast machinery is engine territory" for Cascade, "...the ETB trigger, optional sacrifice, and downstream sacrifice-payoff abilities are engine territory" for Exploit) — a deliberate, repeated MAST scoping decision, not an oversight. The label doesn't even thread which keyword it is (unlike the sibling "evasion" discriminator, which projects evasion:<keyword> — PortGraph.cs EmitPort's totality fallback is `$"emit:{effectType.ToLowerInvariant()}"`, keying on EffectType="keywordAbility" only, never Keyword). Corpus sample (920 HandParsedCards-corpus cards carrying this label, tests/magic-ast-tests/Data/_08_Reporting/card-ports.json) shows the label is GENUINELY a grab-bag over ~190 distinct first-line shapes, dominated (>75%) by keywords that are CR-definitionally INERT to any resource-flow arm — Trample (119, CR 702.19 excess combat-damage assignment), Vigilance (78), Haste (65), Deathtouch (41), Devoid (33), Reach (31), Indestructible (25), Changeling (23), Defender (21), Flash (12) — combat/state-based-action/timing rules modifiers, never a resource emission. Verified against the census's own top-5 (highest comboPopularityMass) example cards directly off oracle-cards.json: Yahenni Undying Partisan=Haste, Kilo Apogee Mind=Haste, Sun Titan=Vigilance, Stuffy Doll=Indestructible, Nyxbloom Ancient=Trample — 5/5 land in the inert bucket; on each of these cards the keyword is incidental flavor, and the card's real combo relevance (Stuffy Doll's damage-redirect trigger, Sun Titan's ETB reanimation, Yahenni's sac ability) comes from a DIFFERENT, separately-projected ability entirely. A genuine flow-relevant minority DOES exist in the long tail — Exploit (ETB optional-sacrifice outlet), Bargain (optional-sacrifice additional cost), Prowess/Soulbond/Cascade/Storm/Extort/Riot — but arming it is blocked on two compounding facts: (1) it is NOT discriminated from the inert majority at the label OR the AST level (identical KeywordAbilityEffect{Keyword} node regardless of which of the ~95 keywords), so any arm keyed on this label alone fabricates false edges across Trample/Vigilance/Haste/etc.; (2) each flow-relevant keyword needs its OWN from-scratch functional AST decomposition (mirroring the real upgrade Undying/Persist already received — TriggeredAbility+ReturnToBattlefieldEffect, not a bare marker) before any label can be minted for it to project — a backlog of ~8-10 individually-shaped parse-track initiatives (one keyword family each), not a single family-shaped mast-worker slice and not projection-only work. Per adding-a-flow-arm.md's parse/interaction split + INTERACTION.md's "parse-inside-engine bridge" + stop conditions ("the parse gap is architectural, not a family-shaped slice → route to the Parse track"): scoped down, did not force an arm; no PortGraph.cs / PortWalkProjection.cs / PortGraphEngine.cs changes — nothing safe to arm here without either fabricating edges under an undiscriminated label or smuggling full CR-702 keyword-semantics reimplementation into the interaction engine (which is PARSE's job per the intra-card/lexical vs cross-card/causal boundary, not the engine's). Re-pick as: (a) a discriminator fix threading Keyword into the label (emit:keyword:<x>, mirroring evasion) as pure legibility — zero new edges alone, or (b) a dedicated parse-track initiative per flow-relevant keyword (Exploit and Bargain are the cheapest — each is a single well-known CR-cited sacrifice-outlet/cost shape), landed BEFORE a matching arm is designed.

effectType.preventable: INVESTIGATED 2026-07-18 (Currency A pass, port-label-census topProjectionGaps): PreventableEffect ('[Inner] unless [player] pays [cost]', Mana Leak / Rhystic Study / Ward / cumulative-upkeep-tax shape, CR 118.9-adjacent) is a WRAPPER structurally identical to the already-projected optional/conditional wrappers (gated recursion into Inner) — but is NOT the same concept as CR 615/611 damage prevention (that is the separately-coarse preventDamage discriminator; see the fog.json gold's modification:prevention stem). Corpus sample (45 HandParsedCards occurrences) shows Inner.EffectType is a GRAB-BAG: sacrifice 20 (44%), counterSpell 20 (44%), loseTheGame/exile/optional/discardCards/tap 1 each. Both dominant sub-shapes dead-end downstream: 'sacrifice' and 'counterSpell' are THEMSELVES independently-coarse EffectType fallbacks (see their own entries in this file) with zero consuming arm in PortGraphEngine.FlowFeasible, and no TriggerEvent exists for a spell being countered. Unwrapping the wrapper alone (mirroring optional/conditional) would create zero new edges — it would just re-attribute the coarse bucket, defeating Currency A's purpose ('one arm lights up every card'). Arming the sacrifice sub-shape for real would require the FIRST general self-removal-as-effect (sacrifice/destroy, as EffectType not CostType) → ltb dies-trigger arm — a foundational death-payoff generalization (today only reachable via the narrower sac-COST→ltb bridge at PortGraphEngine.cs ~line 305, or per-gold declared bridges like Chatterfang/Ruthless Knave) that is its own properly-scoped, judge-verified initiative, not a safe addition to smuggle in under this label. Per adding-a-flow-arm.md anti-patterns + INTERACTION.md stop conditions: scoped down, did not force an arm; consciously left coarse. Re-pick either as a dedicated 'sacrifice'/'destroy' EffectType projection-slice pass, or as a witnessing gold pairing the existing sac-cost→ltb bridge shape.

restriction.OnlyDuringCombat: phase-scoped timing restriction (CR 506 / CR 602.5, Najeela the Blade-Blossom); like OnlyDuringYourTurn/OnlyDuringYourUpkeep it constrains WHEN the ability can be activated, not what resource flows — a combat-confined loop (the extra-combat-phase engine) still repeats within its window, so consciously inert for recall — no flow rule consumes it yet
restriction.Other: baseline coarse fallback (initiative-03 inception 2026-06-15) — no flow rule consumes it yet
